resources.string: Join fellow students for a 5K run along the Charles River Esplanade, starting and finishing at BU Beach. Runners of all levels are welcome, and walkers can take the shorter 2K loop. Water stations will be set up along the route, and free snacks and t-shirts will be handed out at the finish line.

An informal meetup for students interested in Android and iOS development. Two students will give short demos of apps they built with Jetpack Compose and SwiftUI, followed by open discussion and project feedback. Bring your laptop if you want help debugging your own project. Pizza will be provided.

Meet recruiters from over 100 companies hiring for internships and full-time roles in tech, finance, healthcare, and consulting. Bring printed copies of your resume and dress in business casual. A list of attending employers will be posted on Handshake the week before the fair.

Celebrate Halloween with a back to back screening of two classic horror films on the big screen. Costumes are encouraged, and there will be a costume contest between the two movies with prizes for the top three. Free popcorn, candy, and drinks will be available while supplies last.
Center for Computing and Data Sciences

A hands-on beginner workshop covering the basics of machine learning using Python and scikit-learn. You will train a simple classification model on a real dataset and learn how to evaluate its accuracy. No prior ML experience is needed, but basic Python knowledge is recommended. Please bring a laptop with Python installed.
Center for Career Development, 100 Bay State Road

Get one-on-one feedback on your resume from career advisors and alumni volunteers. Each review lasts about 15 minutes and is first come, first served. Bring a printed or digital copy of your resume and a job description you are targeting if you have one.

The BU Jazz Ensemble presents its fall concert featuring jazz standards along with original pieces composed by students. The performance runs about 90 minutes with a short intermission. Admission is free with a valid student ID, and doors open 30 minutes before the show.

A single-day 3v3 basketball tournament open to all students. Teams can register online until November 10, and individual players without a team will be placed on one. Games are 15 minutes long, and the winning team receives championship shirts. Spectators are welcome.

Take a break from midterms with a 30 minute guided meditation and breathing session led by a wellness counselor. The session is beginner friendly and no experience is needed. Cushions and chairs will be provided, so just show up in comfortable clothing.

A six hour hackathon where teams of up to four build a project around the theme of improving student life on campus. Mentors will be available throughout the night to help with design and debugging. Projects are judged at midnight, and the top three teams win prizes. Dinner and late night snacks are included.

Opening night of the annual student art exhibition featuring paintings, photography, sculpture, and digital art from undergraduate and graduate students. Several of the artists will be present to talk about their work. Light refreshments will be served, and the exhibition stays open for three weeks.

Learn practical study techniques like spaced repetition, active recall, and time blocking to prepare for final exams. The workshop includes a short session on building a realistic study schedule for the last weeks of the semester. Handouts and a sample study planner will be provided to all attendees.
